        UFC returns to Madison Square Garden on Saturday. For 10 years, the famed New York City venue has become a regular destination for the mixed martial arts leader. UFC 334 is a worthy successor with its championship double-header. Ciryl Gane makes his first UFC heavyweight title defense against Josh Hokit in the main event. Their paths to the title couldn't be more different, with Gane having more chances than most. Gane failed to capture the title from Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones and Tom Aspinall -- a murderer's row -- before finally becoming undisputed champion by beating Alex Pereira in an interim title fight and later being promoted. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Speaking of Pereira, who likely has no desire to be compared to Hokit, there's an interesting throughline between them. Both men spent exactly 371 days between their UFC debuts and their first title shots. What's more, both those title shots are hosted in MSG. Hokit's ability to draw attention and his collegiate wrestling background have helped narrow the betting gap between him and Gane in the leadup to the fight. 
Oddsmakers are even less certain about the co-main event. Women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison defends her title against the greatest women's MMA fighter of all time, Amanda Nunes. The many mysteries surrounding the fight, including Harrison's recent neck surgery and Nunes' 41-month layoff, make it hard to predict how each fighter will be.
        
            
                How Kayla Harrison recovered from brutal neck surgery to return for dream fight with Amanda Nunes
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
With so much happening on Saturday night, let's look more closely at the full fight card with the latest odds before we get to our staff predictions and picks for the main card that you can consider before hitting the sportsbooks.UFC 334 fight card, oddsOdds via DraftKings (Odds as of Nov. 13)Ciryl Gane (c) -230 vs. Josh Hokit +190, heavyweight titleKayla Harrison (c) -166 vs. Amanda Nunes +140, women's bantamweight titleCaio Borralho -162 vs. Yousri Belgaroui +136, middleweightsUros Medic -155 vs. Kevin Holland +130, welterweightsBilal Hasan -1050 vs. Luis Gurule +675, flyweightsStephen Thompson -142 vs. Charles Radtke +120, welterweightsChris Duncan -185 vs. Drew Dober +154, lightweightsTerrance McKinney -205 vs. Jim Miller +170, lightweightsDonte Johnson -185 vs. Cesar Almeida +154, middleweightsMelquizael Costa -410 vs. Jared Gordon +320, lightweightsBia Mesquita -265 vs. Macy Chiasson +215 women's bantamweightsSamuel Sanches -118 vs. Evan Elder -102, lightweightsJuan Diaz -410 vs. Heili Alateng +320, bantamweightsUFC 334 expert picksWith such a massive main event on tap, the crew at CBS Sports went ahead with predictions and picks for the main card from Brian Campbell, Brent Brookhouse, Shakiel Mahjouri, Michael Mormile and Brandon Wise.
   CampbellBrookhouseMahjouriMormileWiseGane (c) vs. HokitGane TKO4Gane TKO3Gane TKO3Gane TKO3Gane TKO2Harrison (c) vs. NunesNunes UDHarrison UDNunes UDNunes TKO1Harrison SUB4Borralho vs. BelgarouiBorralho UDBorralho UDBorralho UDBorralho UDBorralho UDMedic vs. HollandMedic UDMedic TKO2Holland UDMedic UDMedic KO2Hasan vs. GuruleHasan KO2Hasan KO1Hasan KO1Hasan UDHasan TKO1Records to date31-2635-2235-2230-2227-30Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit predictionsCampbell: As it has been with most UFC title fights involving Gane, his level of success will likely be dictated by his ability to keep his back off of the canvas, especially against a former NCAA Division I All-American wrestler in Hokit. But Gane, who now trains out of Dubai, has put in the work to improve his takedown defense and the longer he can keep this a kickboxing match against the aggressive but still inexperienced Hokit, the more the odds begin to favor him. For whatever Hokit lacks in size or seasoned technique, he typically makes up for with speed and aggression. But Gane is the rare heavyweight who can match his athleticism and cardio, which means the first French-born UFC champion's overall experience advantage should be the difference in the championship rounds. Brookhouse: Gane has considerable advantages in size and striking technique. As impressive as Hokit's grit was in his war with Curtis Blaydes, Blaydes isn't a technical striker on the level Gane is. That kind of face-first aggression is what a striker like Gane loves to see and punish. Hokit has good speed and is very aggressive, but if he can't get Gane to the ground consistently and hold him there, I have trouble seeing a path to victory for him.Mahjouri: I think the odds should be wider. I really struggle to see a path to victory for Hokit. Most people will say it's his wrestling; after all, he's an NCAA Division I All-American. But I think people are holding on too tightly to Gane's struggles against Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou. It's been more than three years since he imploded against them. Hokit's success largely comes down to his athleticism and heart. He's more agile than many lumbering heavyweights and is fearless in his pursuit. It worked against wrestler Curtis Blaydes and knockout artist Derrick Lewis, both of whom, particularly the latter, were shopworn. Gane is a nightmare matchup for Hokit for the same reason Alex Pereira was: the champion is a natural heavyweight with unnatural speed and footwork. Hokit must contend with a bigger, stronger, more technical striker who is just as fast, if not faster, than him. That's a major problem. Hokit's wrestling gives him a better chance than "Poatan" to exploit Gane's vulnerabilities. Gane has been consistently error-prone throughout his career. But looking at the totality of their weapons, this is the champ's fight to lose.
Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes predictionsCampbell: One has to wonder whether the combination of Harrison's extreme weight cut to 135 pounds and the fact that she's fresh off neck surgery will ultimately cancel out the reality that Nunes is returning to the Octagon more than three years removed from her last fight. Either way, this matchup fits all of the qualifications for a women's MMA superfight. And for as much as Harrison has dominated opponents at this weight class with her size, motor and grappling skills, Nunes is simply a different breed of fighter. An accomplished ground practitioner herself, Nunes also holds a striking advantage that threatens to be the biggest hurdle Harrison will have to overcome. Very few fighters can pull off successfully what Nunes is trying to accomplish after being so far removed from active competition. But let's not forget, she's the GOAT for a reason. Look for Nunes' power to be the difference in a competitive 25-minute scrap. Brookhouse: Harrison has cut a ton of weight and recently had neck surgery. Nunes has been retired for three years. If anyone promises you that they know what is going to happen here or how either woman will look in the Octagon, they are lying to you. I tend to lean toward Harrison's ability to get the fight to the ground and grind out some ugly rounds in a fight that likely gets sloppier as it goes on. Nunes' best moments probably look more impressive, but Harrison's consistency might edge her enough rounds to scrape by with a narrow decision win. But this is a near-impossible fight to pick.Mahjouri: If you'd asked me in January, when this fight was originally scheduled, I would've picked Harrison. Nunes was exiting her physical prime when she retired and returning three years later. It is incredibly unlikely that she'll look better after all that time off. However, Harrison's neck injury and surgery could sway things in Nunes' favor. Harrison's neck was in bad enough shape that she contemplated retirement. She's already admitted that the brutal bantamweight cuts are taking years off the former PFL lightweight champion's life. Simply put, I don't know what physical condition Harrison is in. Nunes is the more well-rounded fighter, even at 38, and these new mysteries surrounding Harrison's health are enough for me to side with the former champ.
Caio Borralho vs. Yousri Belgaroui predictionsCampbell: Belgaroui brings legitimate kickboxing credentials and three consecutive knockouts inside the Octagon into this matchup. He also trains with former rival Alex Pereira in Glover Teixeira's Connecticut gym. But let's not overlook what a huge step up in competition this fight is against a legitimate contender in the No. 6 middleweight Borralho. Yes, it remains true that Belgaroui, who holds advantages of four inches in height and five inches in reach, has quickly improved his takedown defense. But Borralho, whose lone UFC defeat came against Nassourdine Imavov, is too well-rounded and capable of winning wherever this fight goes. Borralho has a strong chin and knows how to remain patient and control distance on the feet, which should offset the threat of a knockout that Belgaroui brings. Brookhouse: Borralho has a clear path to victory if he goes back to the fighter who is willing to go for takedowns and hold top control. Belgaroui is a very dangerous kickboxer who has been extremely good at battering overmatched opponents in the UFC, but he has also been taken down plenty. Borralho is a better all-around fighter, and as long as he fight with a smart gameplan, he should cruise to victory.Who wins Gane vs. Hokit, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

        A pair of title fights are set for Saturday when UFC 334 goes down at Madison Square Garden in New York. In the main event, Ciryl Gane will make his first defense of the UFC heavyweight championship when he takes on rising star Josh Hokit.While Gane vs. Hokit is a big fight, the co-main event is one of the most anticipated women's fights in MMA history. Amanda Nunes, the greatest women's MMA fighter ever, returns from retirement as she looks to recapture the bantamweight championship against former Olympian Kayla Harrison.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Elsewhere on Saturday, fireworks are expected when Caio Borralho takes on Yousri Belgaouri. Borralho has exploded on the scene at middleweight with an 8-1 mark since his promotional debut in 2022. Belgaouri has turned heads himself with three knockout wins in his first three appearances. Plus, "The Doctor" is in when Uros Medic makes his latest walk to the Octagon against veteran Kevin Holland. After a brutal KO loss to Punahele Soriano in January 2025, Medic has turned things around quickly -- and violently -- with four straight first-round KO wins. And the newest top flyweight prospect is back in action to open the main card when Bilal Hasan takes on Luis Gurule.
With such an interesting card set for UFC 334, there will no doubt be plenty of interest in the event, including at sportsbooks. With that in mind, we've once again looked at all the event's main card fights to identify our best bets for each.
        
            
                UFC 334: An inside look at Josh Hokit's incredible rise to title challenger in just one year
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
After a strong 4-1 result for our best bets for UFC 333, we are sitting just under .500 at 27-29 for the year. Now we look ahead to this weekend with the goal of getting back in the black, with our only rule remaining that all bets must be at odds of -250 or better. Let's take a look at this week's picks with odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.  Bilal Hasan	vs.	Luis GuruleUnder 1.5 rounds (-175)Bilal Hasan is a pretty massive -1200 favorite and is even -800 at -3.5 on the point spread line. After an impressive showing on Dana White's Contender Series and a knockout in his UFC debut, it's pretty clear that Hasan's being given another chance to impress when he faces Luis Gurule, who is 1-4 since his own appearance on Contender Series. Roughly a quarter of flyweight non-title fights end before the midway point of the second round. Hasan scored one of those early stoppages in his first UFC fight, but that win came at the 2:28 mark of Round 2, coming in just two seconds on the "under" side. Gurule has had a rough go of it in the UFC, and this fight is set up to continue Hasan's rise, so I'll side with him getting it done quickly.
Uros Medic vs.	Kevin HollandUros Medic moneyline (-155)Kevin Holland is one of the trickiest fighters to understand in the game. He can look fantastic using his length and craftiness and also can get dominated by fighters who are dialed in. Holland is 8-10 since 2021, which isn't a great record, but 18 fights since the start of 2021 is a wild career pace. Uros Medic is riding a four-fight knockout streak, most recently taking just 30 seconds to stop Daniel Rodriguez in Serbia. Medic brings big power and a lot of speed, so if he can get inside of Holland's reach, he can likely do some very good work. Medic just needs to stick to the gameplan and not be baited by Holland's antics. If Medic hesitates to move forward, he's in trouble, but I think he has the right style to break Holland down over the course of the fight.Caio Borralho	vs.	Yousri BelgarouiCaio Borralho moneyline (-155)This fight likely comes down to which version of Caio Borralho shows up. Early in his UFC career, we saw Borralho willing to use takedowns and ground control, such as when he scored four takedowns of Armen Petrosyan for more than 10 minutes of control time. Borralho only has one takedown in his five most recent fights. Both styles have worked well for Borralho, who has an 8-1 UFC record, but against Yousri Belgaroui, Borralho will have a far easier time finding his old takedown and ground game style. Belgaroui is a fantastic kickboxer, who has blitzed his UFC competition so far. Even in finding success on the feet, Belgaroui has been taken down plenty in his short UFC career and Borralho is a good enough fighter to take advantage of that skill gap to find a win.Kayla Harrison vs.	Amanda NunesOver 3.5 rounds (+105)Every now and then, you get a fight where the best you can say is, "Man, I don't know." Nunes might be impacted by rust from the time since her retirement. Harrison might also be a bit rusty in recovering from neck surgery. There's no real way to know how those issues factor into how things play out. I lean toward this fight stretching on for a while, however, with both women being a bit out of form and likely cautious of what the other brings to the cage. Harrison will want to score some takedowns and I think she can hold Nunes down, but maybe not find a finish. Around the third round, I expect both women to show some fatigue and things could get a little ugly. I think things are set up to get into the late stages, so I'll go with the over.
Ciryl Gane vs.	Josh HokitCiryl Gane moneyline (-205)Hokit's rise has been admirable, whatever you feel about his behavior outside of the fight. But this is a big jump for him. Gane has been susceptible to takedowns in the past, most notably against Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou. The Ngannou fight is more of a red flag than getting taken down by Jones, but that fight also took place almost five years ago and I think Gane has improved plenty since then. Gane has the size, reach and striking advantage in this fight, so if he can keep from getting taken down, this may be an easy title defense for him. Hokit showed grit and toughness in his war with Curtis Blaydes, but getting into a fight like that against Gane will go badly for him in a hurry. I'm going with the more proven commodity with the better chances of putting out some serious damage in the main event.Who wins Gane vs. Hokit, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

title: UFC 334: An inside look at Josh Hokit's meteoric rise to title challenger - CBS Sports
description: NEW YORK -- Depending upon the time of day or the number of people present when a microphone is placed in front of unbeaten Josh Hokit,
body:
NEW YORK -- Depending upon the time of day or the number of people present when a microphone is placed in front of unbeaten Josh Hokit, you can expect to hear from one of two sides of the rising heavyweight's contrasting personalities.There's Josh, the former Division I All-American wrestler from the blue-collar farmland of California's San Joaquin Valley, who walked on in two sports at Fresno State University and went on to sign with two different NFL teams before transitioning to MMA. Josh is a quiet and calculated competitor of the highest degree who is never lacking for confidence.And then there's "The Incredible Hok." That guy is an obnoxious handful to most and a growing folk hero to an increasingly vocal minority that can't help but pull up a chair and enjoy Hokit's character-driven journey to command our attention at any cost, regardless of the consequences. This crass version of Hokit has boldly navigated the toxic reality of elite MMA, where those who can disrupt the loudest and keep winning can cut the line in pursuit of the sport's greatest riches. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Hokit (10-0) has gone from making his UFC debut last November as a little-known trash talker to headlining Madison Square Garden on Saturday against Ciryl Gane (14-2, 1 NC) at UFC 334. And whether his formula for fast-tracking ends with him becoming the heavyweight champion of the world or not, the last 12 months of Hokit's meteoric rise have been staggering to watch. On Thursday, Hokit turned 29, and he has only been a pro fighter for just over three years. In January, he fought at UFC 324 on the opening bout of the early prelims and just 10 months later -- after co-authoring the craziest fight of 2026 in an April win over Curtis Blaydes and knocking out UFC's all-time KO artist Derrick Lewis at the White House in June -- he's on the verge of legitimate breakout stardom.
This is the type of heater not seen in the UFC since Brock Lesnar won the heavyweight title in 2008 just 287 days after his debut or when Alex Pereira transitioned from kickboxing star to UFC middleweight champion in just 371 days (which, coincidentally, would be the exact amount of time between Hokit's first walk to the Octagon and Saturday's card should he capture the sport's most prestigious title).
"It's no surprise to me," Hokit told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "I keep saying this, but it takes 10 years to make an overnight sensation. So, I have been putting in the work and have been waiting for my opportunity. Every opportunity that the UFC has given me, I have made the most of it, and so now I'm being rewarded for that. We are rewarded by our courage in this life and not our intelligence. And people get that twisted. People will try to have a certain approach, but you need to go for it; you need to put it all on the line. You need to be all or nothing and that's what I'm going for."
        
            
                Ciryl Gane brushes off dirty fighter label, but others are convinced: 'All of these things are illegal'
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Not all of Hokit's comedic material lands, and much of it overshadows his true ability and the purity of his story of overachievement. But whether you respect Josh the person or loathe the cringier side of "The Incredible Hok" as a character, both have relied upon an insane work ethic and a fierce competitive spirit to get Hokit to where he is today.Hokit has accepted opportunities against more proven names on short notice and consistently rolled the dice, believing that his fearlessness and aggression could overcome his lack of experience. 
So far, Hokit's bet on himself has paid off, as he has openly benefited from being an undersized heavyweight who relies on his athleticism and quick hands to surprise and overwhelm his much larger opponents. But that doesn't mean he believes what he's doing is a template that can be easily replicated. 
"If you don't have wrestling, then I wouldn't advise it for a small heavyweight," Hokit said. "At least I have the wrestling in the back pocket, and I think wrestling is the great equalizer. So, I could always fall back on that and make the heavyweights tired. But at the end of the day, it's all about tactics and it's all about strategy. If size always played a factor in the fight, then the elephant would be the king of the jungle."Hokit's unexpected rise has been aided by the constant chaos surrounding the UFC's heavyweight division, which dates back to Francis Ngannou vacating the title in 2023 to leave the promotion as a free agent. Jon Jones returned from a 3-year layoff to win the title but sat out for more than a year due to injury and ended up retiring again in order to avoid fighting then-interim titleholder Tom Aspinall. 
Things only got crazier from there, as accidental eye pokes from Gane in their title bout last year led to Aspinall undergoing multiple surgeries before being forced to vacate the belt two months ago, during a stretch that Hokit calls "unlucky" for the division. Hokit, who is entering his fifth UFC fight in just a 12-month span, believes it's his willingness to be a "rare" active heavyweight that makes him the perfect candidate to save the division. Hokit, who began his shtick of WWE-inspired theatrics during his post-fight interviews on the regional MMA scene, initially turned just about everyone off. He made multiple tasteless jokes about seemingly unrelated celebrities, including crude remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama that drew public chastising from UFC CEO and president Dana White, and even simulated vomiting on himself while weighing in before the Lewis fight in June. 
"I kind of just put my material out there and then it's like, it is what it is," Hokit said. "Whether you like it or not, at least it's something for you to judge because I think that's real important for me. I don't want you to see my name or watch me fight, and then you don't know how you feel about me. I'm just giving everybody a lot to react to. Whether you like it or not, it is what it is."
One month earlier, during a UFC Freedom 250 press conference in Newark, New Jersey, Hokit was ejected by security after his vulgar comments about Ilia Topuria's ex-wife and Alex Pereira's mother nearly sparked fisticuffs with both fighters. Hokit's act may appear foolish and irrational on the surface, thanks to his blatant disregard for shame, but it's all part of his clever strategy to upset the entire sport in pursuit of clout, and it's hard to argue it isn't working. He even wrote the verses for his new diss track titled "MSG Freestyle," which launched complete with a music video, and took shots at the entire division."I'm here to piss people off, No. 1. And I think I'm the shit, No. 2," Hokit said. "So, that's the beauty of this sport, at the end of the day. I'm talking smack, but at least you can do something about it. You could sign the contract and fight me. Shit, if they want to fight me outside, it is what it is. I'm down for all of it. But I think we live in a day and age where people aren't like that anymore. Usually, they will have the opportunity to fight me in the cage in front of the world. We can make some money off of it."
Slowly but surely, however, the court of public opinion within MMA is starting to come around on Hokit, in ways that can be gauged not just by the social media metrics proving that the antihero side of his polarizing personality is rapidly becoming appealing to fans, but also by how many current and former UFC fighters are now openly praising him. From Daniel Cormier, Chael Sonnen and Robert Whittaker to Sean O'Malley, Jorge Masvidal and Dustin Poirier, all of them seem to have endured the same trajectory as many fans. They initially loathed Hokit before eventually coming around to realizing the method to his madness and realizing just how much excitement he brings to the division and the sport. 
"It's a crazy trajectory [Hokit] has been on," Poirier, the retired UFC star and current Paramount+ analyst, told CBS Sports on Monday. "He's walking the walk and talking the talk. When you do that, you become a superstar in this sport. I've said it over and over again. We have seen Paddy [Pimblett], we have seen Chael, we have seen Conor [McGregor]. When you do that, you become a superstar. You just have to keep winning."
Even Gane, who has found himself as the punchline of multiple Hokit zingers entering Saturday, didn't hesitate to share the respect he has for him. "As a man, [I respect him] because I know he likes to pretend that he's dark [but] this is a role, I'm pretty sure," Gane told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "And [I respect him] as a fighter; also, he did very well, 10-0, against good fighters. But he has less experience. This reminds me of when I started, a little bit. You have less experience and maybe you are less technical on the wrestling or the striking game, but you manage very well and you win the fight at the end. So, that means he has a good fight IQ." Hokit doesn't see himself as a hero or a villain when it comes to the multiple personas he has crafted. Love him or hate him, as long as you feel something, he has done his job. 
"I'm whatever the UFC needs. Whatever I am, the UFC needs it," Hokit said. "I just look at it as entertainment."One year ago, almost no one in MMA was talking about Josh Hokit. But on Saturday, in the same building that has been a cathedral of combat sports where former heavyweight champions like Muhammad Ali, Joe Frazier, Evander Holyfield, Lennox Lewis, Andy Ruiz Jr. and Jon Jones have enjoyed some of the biggest moments of their careers, "The Incredible Hok" has the same opportunity to forever link his name with history. "When you got the game upside down, full nelsoned and face on pavement, this is where I belong at the end of the day," Hokit said. "You named all those legends, and I see myself as a living legend already. My third fight in the UFC was a Hall of Fame fight, a legendary fight. So, I believe I've earned this. I've earned a chance to compete here, and I want my name to be with them."

body:
Kentucky needed a last-second 3-pointer to escape what would’ve been a historic loss at home

        Kentucky escaped a near-historic upset loss on Friday against Northern Arizona when guard Alex Wilkins knocked down a 3-pointer to give his team a 78-77 win at home. The Wildcats trailed by four points in the final minute. After NAU missed the front-end of a one-and-one, Wilkins delivered a go-ahead shot to avoid what would've been one of the most stunning losses in Kentucky basketball history. 
Kentucky led by as many as 13 in the first half before Northern Arizona mounted a comeback to take a lead in the final minutes. For the third time in three games, Mark Pope's team struggled. Kentucky were on the ropes against James Madison last week at home before pulling away late. Earlier in the week, Kentucky suffered an embarrassing loss at the Champions Classic where Pope's squad was completely outclassed by the Jayhawks. Even though Kentucky beat NAU — a team that has been at the bottom of KenPom's rankings the last few seasons — it won't ease the pressure on Pope in what is a make-or-break season for his alma mater.
Kentucky entered the 2026-27 season with one of the highest-priced rosters in the sport. Naturally, the expectations were high for the No. 24-ranked Wildcats after adding multiple transfers — including Iowa State sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic — who was the best 3-point shooter in the sport last season. After having one of the highest-priced rosters last season with a price tag reportedly over $20 million, that group underachieved and lost to Iowa State in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. From the moment last season started to the final game, Kentucky had several lowlights, including a 17-point loss to Michigan State, a 35-point loss to Gonzaga and a 25-point defeat against Vanderbilt during SEC play.
Even though Kentucky improved to 3-1 with the win over Northern Arizona on Friday night, it won't cool down the hot seat and the pressure facing Pope this season. Kentucky is expected to drop out of the next AP poll rankings after losing to Kansas. With games coming up against Indiana, Virginia and Louisville during the next month, playing as Kentucky did against NAU will result in a different result in the win-loss column.

body:
On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stoppage for all departing flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety." That announcement came as numerous college football programs were preparing to leave for road games across the country.After a lengthy halt to all air travel, the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday night, but programs still have work to do in order to finalize their travel plans. In his press conference, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy recommended that schools reach out to the FAA about their travel arrangements."I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA to schedule their flight times and make sure they have games going off tomorrow," Duffy said.As of Friday night, there were quite a few teams that haven't taken off, and they are still working on alternative travel plans. That raises another set of questions, including timing and player safety. What if these teams can't get the proper rest after spending most of Friday night on a bus, and will games have to be pushed back due to late arrivals?
Another wrinkle in all this is that on-air talent and behind-the-scenes staff for broadcasts will be affected by the groundstop. 'Wonderboy' returns to the site of his most famous fight for one last showdown

        UFC 334 takes place in Madison Square Garden on Saturday, celebrating 10 years of classic moments in New York City. The promotion's landmark UFC 205 event saw Conor McGregor become the first simultaneous two-division champion. Since then, The World's Most Famous Arena has hosted defining moments like Georges St-Pierre's triumphant return and Jorge Masvidal's BMF coronation.The annual New York City event is a cornerstone of the promotion. This year is no different. Josh Hokit could go from UFC debutant to heavyweight champion in 12 months by dethroning Ciryl Gane in the main event. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Saturday's co-main event is worthy of the iconic New York City venue. Kayla Harrison is one of the most decorated women in combat sports, having won two Olympic gold medals in judo, a UFC title, and two PFL tournaments. Amanda Nunes is unequivocally the best women's MMA athlete of all time. Her resume includes wins over former UFC champions Ronda Rousey, Valentina Shevchenko (twice), Cris Cyborg, Holly Holm, Germaine de Randamie (twice) and Miesha Tate. Many factors are at play, including Harrison's first fight after career-threatening neck surgery and Nunes' return from a three-year retirement.
But Saturday night is about a lot more than just the pair of title fights atop the marquee.
        
            
                UFC 334 fight card -- Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit: Five biggest storylines to follow in New York
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Ahead of Saturday's loaded card, take a look at three undercard fights you can't miss.Stephen Thompson vs. Charles Radtke"Wonderboy" is heading for greener pastures. Two-time UFC title challenger Thompson fights for the final time this weekend. It's a fitting farewell for the 43-year-old, who returns to the same venue where he nearly dethroned welterweight champion Tyron Woodley a decade ago. Their memorable UFC 205 scrap earned Fight of the Night honors and might have been the evening's biggest story had McGregor not closed out the historic triple-header by becoming the UFC's first champ-champ.
Thompson remained a factor at 170 pounds for years after his two title fights with Woodley, but three straight losses signaled that his time was running out. UFC matchmakers have given him a reasonable opportunity to leave on a high note. Charles Radtke is solid competition with a 5-2 UFC record, losing only to ranked welterweights Carlos Prates and Mike Malott. Can Thompson find that "Wonderboy" magic one last time, or will he share the cruel fate that many beloved fighters do in the twilight of their careers?
Caio Borralho vs. Yousri BelgarouiBorralho is taking a considerable risk. The UFC's No. 6-ranked middleweight is coming off a victory over Reinier de Ridder, his eighth win in nine Octagon appearances. Borralho should be climbing towards a title shot, but he's agreed to defend his place among the division's elite against an unranked opponent. And not just any unranked opponent.
Belgaroui is cut from the same cloth as former UFC champions Alex Pereira and Israel Adesanya. The Dutch striker fought both men twice in kickboxing before transitioning to MMA. He now trains alongside Pereira under Glover Teixeira's tutelage. Belgaroui is a perfect 3-0 in the UFC, with all three victories coming by knockout. He's following a familiar blueprint, and Madison Square Garden is the perfect place for it. Pereira made his UFC debut at the Garden in 2021 before returning the following year to win the middleweight title. Now it's Belgaroui's turn to make a statement in NYC. But Borralho is a considerable obstacle. The Fighting Nerds' cerebral leader has the tools and experience to expose gaps in Belgaroui's developing MMA game. It's a difficult assignment for both men, albeit for very different reasons.Bilal Hasan vs. Luis GuruleHasan might be the best talent to emerge from this year's crop of "Dana White's Contender Series" graduates. "The IndoNinja" punched his ticket to the UFC with a 45-second knockout, then returned just two weeks later to score another KO in his promotional debut. Saturday marks his third fight in three months under the UFC umbrella. The young flyweight has finished nearly everyone he's faced, and should be due for another one.
Hasan hovers around a staggering -1000 favorite against Gurule, who has struggled to a 1-4 UFC record. Some might question why such an apparent mismatch belongs on a Madison Square Garden main card, but there are things to like about it. Talent development hasn't historically been the UFC's strong suit. The promotion touts competitive matchmaking, but that philosophy sometimes comes at the expense of rushing prodigies into fights they're not ready for. Hasan has the makings of a future champion, and there's no reason to hurry him towards the division's elite. Let him build his experience, collect highlights and develop into the fighter he has the potential to be. Saturday is the next step in his story.
Honorary mentions: Uros Medic vs. Kevin Holland, Drew Dober vs. Chris Duncan, Jim Miller vs. Terrance McKinneyWho wins Gane vs. Hokit, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

After successfully defending the interim belt against Julian Williams, Adames was promoted to full champion after Jermall Charlo was stripped of his title.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch Zuffa Boxing 13 for no additional fee -- along every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Since becoming full champion, Adames has retained the title win a win over Terrell Gausha, a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz and a win over Austin "Ammo" Williams. Adames joins Aaron McKenna, who won the IBF title at Zuffa Boxing 10, as middleweight world champions under Zuffa control.Warburton is a step down in competition for Adames. Adames is far and away the best fighter Warburton has faced in his career.Warburton will enter Saturday's fight on a three-fight winning streak since a fourth-round TKO loss to Kieron Conway. Two of those recent victories came against fellow Englishman Nathan Heaney.
Also of note on Saturday, former WBO bantamweight champion Jason Moloney makes his Zuffa Boxing debut when he takes on Andres Teran at 118 pounds. Moloney lost a pair of hard-fought decisions against Yoshiki Takei and Tenshin Nasukawa that cost him his WBO crown. He then bounced back with a pair of wins over lower-level competition. But now he looks to get back in the spotlight with a win over Teran, who is 19-2 with 14 knockouts on his resume. Teran has yet to truly step up his level of competition, however. Let's take a closer look at the rest of the fight card set for Saturday night in Saudi Arabia before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.Zuffa Boxing 13 fight cardCarlos Adames vs. Gerome Warburton, super middleweightsAndres Teran -125 vs. Jason Moloney -106, bantamweightsBruno Surace vs. Kamil Bednarek, super middleweightsRadzhab Butaev vs. Alexander Castro, middleweightsIvan Ortiz vs. Dariial Kuchmenov, lightweightsRakhmatullo Boymatov vs. Moro Inusah Kanla, light heavyweightsJakhongir Zokirov vs. Brandon Colantonio, heavyweightsRayan Awaji vs. Sudais Lubega, welterweightsAbdualaziz Alotebi vs. Ezra Ssaili, featherweightsPredictionThere's not much mystery to how this fight is likely to play out. Adames has been proving himself against elite middleweights for years, while Warburton has not sniffed the world championship level. That's not to take a shot at Warburton, who is a solid B-tier fighter, but rather to set a base level of expectations.
Adames should cruise on Saturday, with the bigger question being how Adames looks moving up a division to super middleweight. It's unlikely Adames sticks at super middle, but it could be a bit of a glimpse into the future.Adames is a better boxer, better puncher and more experienced at an elite level. Warburton has was stopped by Conway, who has just seven stoppage wins in 23 career victories, after Warburton's corner threw in the towel. There's no reason to expect Adames can't find the finish by attacking the body the same way Conway did. Pick: Carlos Adames via TKO5

Their relationship, forged through triumphs and failures, has strengthened in recent years as Sarkisian helped Kiffin work through sobriety and improve his personal life off the field. On Saturday night, the old friends reunite, each trying to eliminate the other from the College Football Playoff race. No. 21 LSU, fresh off its first home loss under Kiffin, is trying to avoid dropping home games in consecutive weeks for the first time since 1994. No. 6 Texas has won six straight games against ranked opponents, the longest active streak in the FBS. The loser may very well be eliminated from playoff contention. It's one of five ranked-on-ranked matchups in a week built for more chaos. A top-two team has lost in five straight weeks, tying 2007 for the longest stretch in AP Top 25 history. 
No. 1 Georgia hosts No. 22 Missouri, which has never beaten an AP No. 1 team in 18 tries. No. 2 Utah, one of two unbeaten FBS teams remaining, visits No. 23 Arizona as a slight favorite against the Wildcats. Both of Arizona's wins over top-10 teams since 2015 came against the Utes, and starting quarterback Noah Fifita is 2-0 against them. On CBS, No. 9 Indiana hosts No. 18 USC, with the Hoosiers fighting for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game and the Trojans trying to stay alive in the playoff race. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover is off the injury report, but leading rusher Turbo Richard is out. A loss would all but end USC's playoff hopes. Meanwhile, No. 12 Texas Tech visits No. 25 Oklahoma State in the Dust Bowl. Conference races are still in flux, but Georgia can clinch a spot in the final SEC Championship Game on Saturday with a win and some help. 
Let's get to our experts' Week 11 picks. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, whose 872 rushing yards rank as the second most in the NFL this season, popped up on the injury report on Friday after tweaking his groin, causing him to not practice on the final day of the week."We're feeling it out just to see. We're not going to put him at risk," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Friday, via ESPN. "If he can go, he'll go. If he can't, he can't."  Some believe new Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s absence in Week 9 at the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury is somehow connected to his lack of a new contract in the final year of his rookie deal. However, Porter Jr. (ankle) made it clear that isn't the case on Thursday. He called his entire foot, heel and ankle "jacked up." He also said the determination on whether he will play against the San Francisco 49ers will be made after practice on Friday and based on how he feels on Sunday. Porter Jr. didn't practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a limited participant on Friday. That's why the Cowboys listed him as questionable for Week 10. 
"That has no, I don't even know where that narrative comes from. I get it, it's the internet. I don't really pay attention to that. I don't really care for that," Porter Jr. said after practice on Thursday. "My goal is to win games and play football. That's what I want to do. If there's any chance I can get on the field, I'm going to get on the field and do what I do best."     Below, we will break down the final injury reports for all teams set to play on Sunday, beginning with our international game in Munich, GermanyOdds courtesy of DraftKings SportsbookNew England Patriots at Detroit Lions in Munich (-2.5)Patriots: C Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) OUT; WR A.J. body:
The FAA groundstop on Friday caused travel issues for many teams, including the Rebels, who were facing issues getting to Oklahoma
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:05 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma's efforts to block the SEC from rescheduling its home matchup against Ole Miss to Sunday ended in defeat after a nationwide flight groundstop and a Friday night dispute with conference officials.SEC commissioner Greg Sankey moved the Sooners' home game against No. 19 Ole Miss in Norman, Oklahoma, from Saturday afternoon to Sunday at 1 p.m. ET (noon CT) a decision Oklahoma athletics director Roger Denny said came "over our strong objection." When OU attempted to keep the game Saturday, Sankey told the school that failing to play at the directed time would result in a forfeit."Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner Nation," Denny said in a statement released early Saturday. "But we've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening."
Ole Miss administrators couldn't secure a charter flight from Tupelo, Mississippi, to Oklahoma City after the groundstop, and the earliest they could book another flight was Saturday at 4:20 p.m., a team spokesperson told CBS Sports.
The trouble began Friday afternoon, when air travel across the country stopped. The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports shortly before 3 p.m. CT after communication problems hit multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, the facilities that manage high-altitude traffic between airports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed switches and routers that became overloaded and shut down after they began producing inconsistent data. Thousands of flights were delayed or canceled before the FAA lifted the order at 7:15 p.m. CT, more than four hours after it began. It was only the third full groundstop in the country's history.Most college football teams do not travel to game sites until the day before games, leaving many scrambling after the groundstop was ordered. All games in the FBS managed to stay on Friday and Saturday, with Ole Miss' trip to Oklahoma the only exception. Kick times across the country were slightly altered, including No. 2 Utah's game at No. 23 Arizona, which is now set to begin at 10:30 p.m. ET on Saturday after the Utes were unable to leave Salt Lake City Friday.Ole Miss and Auburn were among four SEC teams grounded for several hours. Auburn's game at Mississippi State was moved to 3:15 p.m. CT Saturday as the Tigers left an airport and booked buses for a four-hour road trip to Starkville. No. 6 Texas was delayed until after 10 p.m. CT until boarding a flight to play No. 21 LSU on Saturday.
Every other traveling SEC team found a way, including Tennessee, which managed to reschedule a flight after the groundstop for its longest road trip of the season at Texas A&M. Ole Miss players were sent home Friday afternoon and told to return to the football facility that evening for updates. Ole Miss flies out of Tupelo, Mississippi, a 55-minute drive from Oxford, and flies about 90 minutes to Oklahoma City."We are continuing to work through our options and coordinate with the appropriate groups regarding both travel and the game," an Ole Miss spokesperson told CBS Sports earlier Friday.
Ole Miss wanted to play Sunday and Oklahoma wanted to keep the game Saturday, CBS Sports reported Friday night. The league sided with the Rebels."We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned," Denny said. "But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution."The game had been scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT Saturday on SEC Network. Television plans for Sunday have not been announced.
"Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans," Denny said. "Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight."Oklahoma (5-4, 4-4 SEC)  is coming off a 23-7 win at Florida in Jason Witten's first game as interim offensive coordinator. The Sooners need one more win to reach bowl eligibility.Ole Miss (6-3) fell to No. 19 in the College Football Playoff rankings after a 42-7 home loss to now-No. 1 Georgia. 
"We will continue to fight in the best interests of OU Athletics and always on behalf of our student-athletes and fans," Denny said.
